hook.line: When two houses are on the same street, you point: the one with the red roof. Spanish lets you drop the noun and keep only the little word and a describing bit.
hook.en: I want the one that has a balcony.

examples.es:
¿Cuál es tu casa?
La que tiene el techo rojo.
examples.en:
Which one is your house?
The one with the red roof.

examples.es: Mi hermana es la que está hablando con Pablo.
examples.en: My sister is the one who's talking to Pablo.

examples.es: Vale es la que hace el pan.
examples.en: Vale is the one who makes the bread.
I prefer the one that has a window.

examples.es: Los que viven aquí conocen a Hernando.
examples.en: The ones who live here know Hernando.
Those who want to come, let me know. (to you all)

rule:
To say the one that…, don't repeat the noun. Keep the article and add *que*:
*el que*, *la que*, *los que*, *las que*.

*La casa que tiene balcón* becomes *la que tiene balcón*.

The article must match the noun you dropped: *la casa*, so *la que*; *los carros*, so *los que*. Never drop the article: *que tiene balcón* alone doesn't work.

It's useful for answering *¿cuál?* and for naming a person by what they do: *Vale es la que hace el pan.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a relative pronoun with an article, replacing a noun that was already understood.

readAndPick.es: La que tiene el techo rojo.
options: The one with the red roof (a house or a place).
The ones with the red roof.
I prefer the one that has a window (a room or a place).
I prefer the ones that have a window.

readAndPick.es: Los que viven aquí conocen a Hernando.
options: The one who lives here knows Hernando.
The ones who live here know Hernando.

readAndPick.es: Vale es la que hace el pan.
options: Vale is the one who makes the bread.
Vale is the one who sells the bread.
I want the one that has a balcony.
I want the ones that have a balcony.

readAndPick.es: Las que están en la mesa son mis llaves.
options: The ones on the table are my keys.
The one on the table is my key.

readAndPick.es: Simón es el que habla mucho.
options: Simón is the one who talks a lot.
Simón is the one who talks little.

readAndPick.es:
¿Cuál es Mariana?
La que escribe en el periódico.
options:
Which one is Mariana?
The one who writes for the newspaper.

Who is Mariana?
The one who reads the newspaper.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *el que* or *la que* and type the whole sentence: *Quiero ___ tiene balcón.* (I want the one that has a balcony; talking about a house, *la casa*.)
Pick *el que* or *los que* and type the whole sentence: *___ viven aquí conocen a Hernando.* (The ones who live here know Hernando.)
yourTurn.answer: Los que viven aquí conocen a Hernando.
yourTurn.why: More than one person, so *los que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale is the one who makes the bread.
yourTurn.answer: Vale es la que hace el pan.
yourTurn.why: Vale is a woman, so *la que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I prefer the one that has a window.
yourTurn.why: Dropped noun is masculine, like *cuarto*, so *el que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Simón is the one who talks a lot.
yourTurn.answer: Simón es el que habla mucho.

yourTurn.prompt: Answer, giving the house with the red roof: *¿Cuál es tu casa?*
yourTurn.answer: La que tiene el techo rojo.
accept: Es la que tiene el techo rojo.
yourTurn.why: You drop *casa* but keep *la*, then *que* and what describes it.

yourTurn.prompt: Shorten it by dropping the noun: *Quiero la casa que tiene balcón.*
yourTurn.why: Cut the noun, keep the article and *que*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Don't drop the article: *la que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Prefiero la que tiene ventana, el cuarto.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The article matches the dropped noun: *cuarto* is masculine, so *el que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Vale es que hace el pan.
pitfalls.right: Vale es la que hace el pan.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *es* you still need the article: *la que*.

personal: Describe someone you know without their name: *Mi amigo es el que…* or *Mi hermana es la que…*.
